newsitem.title: USA: UAW engine plant workers approve contract.
newsitem.headline: UAW engine plant workers approve contract.

text.p: United Auto Workers union members overwhelmingly approved a new contract with Chrysler Corp., putting an end to a month-long strike at the company's Mound Road Engine plant.

The vote was 1,009 in favor and 182 against. More than 1,850 UAW members from Local 51 walked off the job shortly before midnight April 9 in a strike that disrupted production of some of Chrysler's most profitable vehicles -- full-sized pickups and sport utility vehicles.

Union members approved the contract despite noisy dissent from several angry union members who accused bargainers of settling the strike too quickly. Some members may start returning to work as early as Friday night but production is not expected to start until next week.

UAW leaders told members that production of drive shafts will remain in the plant, contradicting information from Chrysler and some auto industry analysts. The union had said shifting the work to outside contractors could have cost up to 300 jobs.

Chrysler also has agreed to invest $75 million to upgrade the facility, including installing a new engine block production line. Workers also will be able to transfer to the company's new Mack Avenue Engine plant.
